cands.how: Crushed rock grinding under the weight: the packs' real gravel-crunch steps (sfx_100 footstep_01/02, a slice from a different crunch each take) pitched down a little for fist-sized stones, lower stone grains filling it out under them, and a dull pad of weight. Outdoors, dry. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on the ballast of the track bed

cands.how: Coal lumps are brittle and glassy: a slice of the packs' real stones knocking, a burst of hard little grains breaking and clinking with them as the weight comes on (front-loaded), a dull pad of weight, and a few lumps sliding down the pile after. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on the coal in the tender

cands.how: Hard boots on stone, rebuilt after the director's "super weird squishy footstep" (8 Oct; the packs' concrete steps were soft soles, a low wobble): each heel and toe the sole's crack on rock (a few ms of noise from 1.5 kHz up), the stone's dead knock (broad modes at 0.4-2.3 kHz, gone in 20 ms), a short thump of weight, the boot's sole click, and sand between the setts. Outdoors, dry. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on cobbles and stone setts, outdoors

cands.how: The same hard boot on smoother stone (less sand), in a short hard indoor room. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on an indoor concrete floor

cands.how: Soft ground takes the click out of a boot: Kenney's dull wooden step lowpassed as the earth's thud, the boot recording lowpassed under it, and a fine grit of sand and needles. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on packed dirt and forest floor

cands.how: Kenney's grass steps (the blades swishing aside) as each contact, a thin rustle of stalks for variety, and the boot lowpassed as the soft ground under it. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots in grass and heath

cands.how: Each heel and toe is Kenney's thin plate hit, choked fast where the boot stops it, a short ring of light metal pitched down, and two to four tiny clicks of the bars chattering in their frame; the boot's sole click (the boot recordings high-passed) on top. Kept free of low boom: a grate is open. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on an open steel grate (running boards, steps, the coupler plates)

cands.how: The packs' wet steps darkened and cut to their squelch, a lower synthesised suction squelch and a dull heavy pad as the boot sinks, and on the toe the suck of the sole pulling out. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots in mud and bog

cands.how: Kenney's medium and heavy plate hits, pitched down a little and choked at once (thick plate under a boot's weight goes dead), a faint ring of metal an octave down, the boot's sole click and a pinch of coal grit, in the cab's small iron room. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on the cab's solid iron footplate and the tender deck

cands.how: A sheet of tin over a hollow car: Kenney's thin plate hit pitched down and only lightly damped, a tin ring pitched down a fifth and kept quiet, the panel's low boom (a 96 Hz drum mode), and the sole's click. Outdoors, dry. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on a car's tin roof

cands.how: The packs' real boot-on-boards recordings (Kenney RPG footsteps) cut into heels and toes and recombined evenly: heel, then the toe 70-90 ms later and 5 dB under it. A little more of the boards' low knock and their low mode for a car floor over a hollow, and the car's small wooden room. Six takes, each heel and toe from a different pair, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on a car's plank floor

cands.how: Rebuilt after AU1's audit (note 419; the boot recordings on boards sat near 300 Hz, the cobbles' old squish): each heel and toe the sole's crack (the boot recording above 1.4 kHz), the board's dry knock (broad woody modes at 0.5-1.7 kHz, gone in 30 ms), the joists' short thump (130 Hz, 15 ms, no boom) and the boot recording itself kept above its wobble, a board creaking now and then off the toe; the car's small wooden room. Six takes, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on a car's plank floor: a hard boot on deal

cands.how: Rebuilt after the same audit (note 419; the old roof was the panel's boom over all of it): the sheet first, Kenney's light plate barely pitched and choked under the boot, a short oil-can pop as it buckles, the loose sheet rattling on its nails, the tin's ring short, and the car's hollow under it, quieter and shorter. Outdoors, dry. Six takes, walked in a steady gait in the preview.
cands.label: Walking: boots on a car's tin roof: the sheet buckling and rattling

current: Its own sounds play in the game now (each cue's first candidate, rough, until you keep one), hooked to what the game's state says happens. Every player's steps, one per stride, walk or run by speed, on the surface under their feet (car floors, grates, plate, roof tin, coal, and the ground off the train from the art's own choice: ballast, dirt, grass, mud, cobbles). The stones (8 Oct, queue #91): after your "super weird squishy footstep sound when I walk on the stones in the town", the cobbles (the streets, the halts' platforms) and the concrete (inside the buildings) are rebuilt as hard boots on stone: each heel the sole's crack on rock and the stone's short dead knock, where before it was a soft sole's low wobble. They're in the game; the old ones are gone. And the rest of the ground (App. F.1, build 1121: "footsteps on the ground sound wrong; on wood and grates they're good"): dirt and grass were a boom a step (the packs' steps lowpassed, two slow swings under 60 Hz), ballast a hiss with no heel, mud half sub. Now dirt is a short dead tup with dry crumbs and needles crunching, grass its swish over a soft tup, ballast a stone heel under the crunch, mud the squelch with the boom taken out.
name: Footsteps by surface
need: Boots on roof tin, cab plate, car boards, ballast and yard ground; walking and running.
notes: These need to be loopable and consistent. There are many more footstep surfaces in this game as well. Note 419 (queue #155): the car floor and roof rebuilt, new candidates beside the old boots: planks (a hard boot on deal: the heel crack, the board knock, the joists short) and tin (the sheet buckling and rattling, the hollow under it). The roof's tin is installed; the floor's planks are a candidate only (you liked the boards as they are, build 1121), there for you to compare.
